messages:
maria: Quick sync — onboarding LoRA for customer 'Bermuda' on top of redwood/galena-13b (4-bit quant). Smoke pack failing consistency for currency extraction (amounts getting rounded or invented). Anyone seen this pattern?
raj: I saw something similar on a separate finetune yesterday — tokenizer special tokens can shift numeric spans after merge. Did we remap <AMT> token?
sophia: Not remapped intentionally. The LoRA uses an extra sentinel token set; merge script should have mapped to existing ids but will double-check.
drew: Can you paste a failing example?
maria: Sure — sample from smoke set: 
```
User: "Total due: $12.34"
Model: "Amount: $13"
```
Also another: 
```
User: "Invoice: 1,250.00 EUR"
Model: "Invoice: 125000 EUR"
```
Weird scaling/decimal shift.
raj: That second one looks like a comma-parsing/tokenization join. If LoRA introduced a new BPE merge, decimals might be split differently across the prefix.
sophia: I pushed a quick token dump. See output: 
```
input_tokens: ["Invoice", ":", " ", "1", ",", "250", ".", "00", " ", "EUR"]
merged_tokens_after_lora: ["Invoice", ":", " ", "125000", " ", "EUR"]
```
So the merge ended up fusing "1"," ,","250" into a single token.
drew: That's consistent with a differing vocab/merges table coming from the LoRA conversion step. Did we run the merge_vocabs step in the pipeline?
maria: Pipeline shows step ran, but maybe the script used `overwrite=true` and prioritized LoRA merges. I can re-run with `--prefer-base-vocab`.
sophia: Before re-running full build, quick test: run evalpack with `tokenize_debug=true` for 50 examples to confirm distribution. I can start that.
ci-bot: build/bermuda-lora/merge-check started by sophia — job #8421. Logs will appear in ~2m.
sophia: Running now. If we confirm it's vocab merges, simplest fix is to remap LoRA merges to base BPE and re-quantize. That should be fast.
raj: Also add a targeted unit test for "digit+comma+triplet" patterns in our smokepack. Prevents regression.
drew: Good call. I'll PR: add test + pipeline flag to prefer base merges.
maria: After that, we should re-run the quick eval diff on the 5 customer-critical prompts (invoices, totals, currency conversions). If perf holds, ship to canary.
sophia: Evalpack results came in — 50 examples token_debug shows 12 affected cases (24%). I'm attaching short diff in the job logs. Initial accuracy drop on numeric extraction: 0.96 -> 0.78.
raj: Oof. Blocker until we fix vocab mapping. Does reverting the LoRA merge locally (apply adaptor but reuse base tokenizer) restore numbers?
maria: I ran that locally — applying adaptor weights but forcing base tokenizer yields 0.95 numeric extraction. So adaptors are fine, it's definitely tokenizer merges.
drew: Timeline: quick patch (remap merges) + re-quantize = ~2-3 hours. Then smokepack + canary. I'll own the PR.
sophia: I'll keep job running and coordinate with QA for a fast rerun. @maria ping me if you want the intermediate artifacts. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks team. Marking this thread for follow-up once PR merges. CI job: #8421 will post final logs.
ci-bot: build/bermuda-lora/merge-check succeeded — job #8421 (logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/8421)
raj: Nice, canary plan after merge: 10% traffic for 12h, monitor token-level diff + amount accuracy metric.
sophia: I'll add alert if numeric-extract accuracy falls below 0.9 during canary.
drew: PR opened: https://phabricator.redwood.ai/D12345 — includes test, pipeline flag, and remediation script.
maria: Closing loop: once canary passes, schedule customer deploy for next maintenance window. Thanks everyone.
